newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet to meet Falconbridge, SMSP May 2.
newsitem.headline: Eramet to meet Falconbridge, SMSP May 2.

text.p: Eramet said on Wednesday its management will meet with the presidents of Canadian group Falconbridge Ltd and Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) on May 2 to discuss plans to build a new nickel plant in the north of New Caledonia.
"There will be a meeting on Friday in Paris," a spokesman for the company told Reuters.
But he said details over the exact time and location of the meeting were still sketchy.
It was also unclear if representatives from state holding Erap would attend the meeting.
Last week Eramet chairman Yves Rambaud offered to meet with the management of Falconbridge and SMSP to discuss the project.
The management of Eramet has come under strong pressure from the government, its main shareholder, over plans to distribute mining assets in the French territory.
The government has already begun a process to withdraw Eramet's mining licence for the Koniambo mine in New Caledonia, saying Eramet had not operated the mine for 10 years.
Under the plan, the Koniambo reserves would be used to supply the plant which Falconbridge and the local Kanak group SMSP plan to build in the north of the island.
The project is part of a deal to appease Kanak separatists ahead of a referendum on independence for the French territory.
Eramet has criticised the plan, saying it was unjustified and would hurt its development in New Caledonia.

Eramet has said it wanted all parties involved to sit down and work on a solution. Last week chairman Yves Rambaud said talks must clarify several issues, including how much ore would be needed to supply the plant, how much SMPS would be able to provide, and how much Eramet would need to bring in.
He also said Eramet was ready to supply the plant and work on a plan to swap assets with SMPS as long as the terms of the exchange were fair.
Company sources said the May 2 meeting was expected to focus on these issues.
